w:r.w:t: Schedule Page — Unified Appointments & Walk-In Queue
Admin, Co-Admin, Secretary, Branch Manager, Owner, Dentist

Currently, appointments and walk-in queue are managed on two completely separate pages per role. This causes unnecessary navigation context-switching when staff need to see the full picture of who is coming in on a given day.

This plan describes the implementation of a new unified Schedule page that merges both views into a single, date-centered interface. The default date filter is always set to today, giving staff an immediate daily snapshot when they open the page.

The table design for this page (and all other tables in the system) will be updated to match a cleaner, more modern style — tabbed status filters with count badges, a date picker, a search bar, colored status pills, and paginated rows in a single-line-per-row layout.
One page. One date. All patient traffic — booked appointments and walk-ins — visible together.

The table styling should match the clean, minimal aesthetic shown in the reference image. Key visual rules:
White background for the table container with a subtle card shadow
Light gray header row (#F1F5F9) with bold blue column labels
Row hover: very light blue background (rgba(1, 83, 139, 0.03))
No text wrapping in any cell — all data on a single line
Horizontal scroll inside the table wrapper when columns exceed viewport
Status values are displayed as small pill/badge elements, not plain text
Patient avatar (32px circle) displayed left of name in the Patient column
Action buttons are small icon buttons, not full-width text buttons
One shared SchedulePage component is used by all roles. Behavior differences are controlled internally via the useAuth() hook (role and assignedBranch).
Appointments: fetched from the existing /surgeries (appointments) API endpoint, filtered by the selected date
Walk-ins: fetched from the existing /queue API endpoint, always scoped to today (queue is inherently a daily concept)
Both datasets are fetched simultaneously on page load and on date change using Promise.all for efficiency
Walk-ins auto-refresh every 30 seconds (setInterval) for roles that manage the queue — this replaces the kanban auto-refresh behavior
Changing the date filter only re-fetches appointments; walk-ins always show today's queue
Because the queue is a real-time, same-day concept, the Walk-ins tab always shows today's data even if the date picker is set to a different day. The date picker only affects the Appointments tab.
